coverage: Read in full: server/services/crm/automationRuleEngine.ts 1-711, crm/customerIdService.ts 1-296, crm/eventService.ts 1-151, crm/messagingService.ts 1-280, crm/recommendationService.ts 1-184, crm/segmentationService.ts 1-227, customerAutomationService.ts 1-454, dailyDigestService.ts 1-354, dailyScheduler.ts 1-127, deviceAttendanceService.ts 1-244, feedbackService.ts 1-294, loyaltyService.ts 1-158, orderPricing.ts 1-89. Cross-checked callers in server/routes.ts (order create CRM hooks, payment route, dues e-bill, CRM profile/sync routes), server/growthRoutes.ts (feedback submit), server/index.ts (schedulers), outboundQueue.enqueueWhatsApp/isSuppressed, inboundService STOP handling, automationStore opt-out, client useCrmExtrasSync/CustomerDashboard, and shared/schema (orderItems.quantity real, feedback.rating integer). Not verified: driver internals, storage.* attendance helpers, shared/shiftTime detectSessions.

findings.title: Public feedback submit issues a ₹100 recovery coupon before an unconditional write; a non-integer rating re-issues coupons without limit
findings.detail: submitFeedback validates only `rating < 1 || rating > 5`, so 2.5 (or NaN, or a non-integer npsScore) passes. It then calls issueCoupon (rating <= 3) BEFORE updating the feedback row, and that UPDATE is unconditional (no `WHERE submitted_at IS NULL`). feedback.rating and nps_score are `integer` columns, so a value like 2.5 makes the UPDATE throw: the route returns 500, submittedAt stays NULL, and the coupon that was already issued is kept. The same token can be replayed indefinitely. Separately, two near-simultaneous submits (a double tap on the public page) both pass the `row.submittedAt` check and both issue a coupon.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone with a feedback link POSTs /api/feedback/<token>/submit with {rating: 2.5} in a loop. Each call issues a new SORRY ₹100 flat coupon, then fails the UPDATE, so the link never locks. A normal customer double-tapping Submit on a 2-star rating gets two coupons.
findings.suggested_fix: Require Number.isInteger(rating) (and an integer npsScore in 0..10). Claim the row first with a conditional `UPDATE feedback SET submitted_at=now(), rating=… WHERE id=$1 AND submitted_at IS NULL RETURNING id`, and issue the coupon only when the claim returned a row (or do both in one transaction).
findings.reason: Confirmed: submitFeedback only range-checks rating; route passes Number(rating); feedback.rating/nps_score are integer columns so 2.5 throws at UPDATE after issueCoupon already inserted a coupon; no WHERE submitted_at IS NULL so concurrent submits both issue. Downgraded: the 500 path never returns the code to the caller, so replay only spams coupons bound to the customer; double-submit yields two usable codes.

findings.title: Customers-page background sync overwrites DB profiles, including a WhatsApp STOP opt-out, with stale localStorage values
findings.detail: CustomerDashboard mounts useCrmExtrasSync, which POSTs the device's whole localStorage `bagicha_customer_extras` map to /api/crm/sync-extras. syncLocalStorageExtras → upsertCustomerProfile writes EVERY field from that stale payload, defaulting missing ones (`doNotSendUpdate ?? false`, `notificationEnabled ?? true`, email/dob/... → null). inboundService sets customer_profiles.doNotSendUpdate=true when a customer replies STOP, and edits made on another device also live only in the DB. Neither is in this device's localStorage, so every page mount reverts them.
findings.failure_scenario: A customer replies STOP, so doNotSendUpdate=true in the DB. Later the owner opens Customers on the desktop, whose localStorage still has that customer's extras with doNotSendUpdate:false. Three seconds later the flag is false again. buildSnapshots (the daily rule engine, which reads only customer_profiles and sends directly through the driver) messages them again. A DOB edited on a phone is likewise reverted by the desktop's old copy.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the bulk sync non-destructive: only insert profiles that don't exist yet, or merge only fields present in the payload and never lower doNotSendUpdate from true to false. Better still, drop the mount-time push and make the DB the source of truth that the client reads.
findings.reason: Confirmed: useCrmExtrasSync posts the full localStorage map on mount; upsertCustomerProfile writes every field with defaults (doNotSendUpdate ?? false). Client keys are dateOfBirth/dateOfAnniversary while payload reads dob/anniversary, so those are nulled too. inboundService STOP writes only DB. conversations.optedOut still blocks the queue path, but the rule engine and other paths read doNotSendUpdate only.

findings.title: Rule engine and settlement fallback send through the WhatsApp driver directly, bypassing the outbound queue's opt-out check and maxPerDay cap
findings.detail: runAutomationServerSide calls messagingService.sendMessage, which uses `driver.sendText` whenever a driver is connected. dispatchSettlement does the same whenever whatsappAutoSend is off (or getDriver() is null at enqueue time but connected in sendMessage). These paths never run outboundQueue.isSuppressed (conversations.optedOut + doNotSendUpdate) and are not counted against maxPerDay. The rule engine's only opt-out check is buildSnapshots' `masterMap.get(key)` profile lookup, keyed on the exact customers_master.key. That misses a STOP recorded against the phone-matched canonical row when the order key differs (name-keyed master, or a duplicate master; see the resolveCustomerId finding). triggerSettlementMessage → buildSnapshotForKey checks no opt-out at all.
findings.failure_scenario: A customer replied STOP (conversations.optedOut=true) and the Baileys host is connected with whatsappAutoSend=false. At their next settlement, triggerSettlementMessage → dispatchSettlement → sendMessage → driver.sendText sends a THANK_YOU anyway. The 10am rule-engine run sends up to 50 direct messages that are not counted toward maxPerDay.
findings.suggested_fix: Route every automated WhatsApp send through enqueueWhatsApp (or call the same isSuppressed + daily-cap check inside sendMessage for automated triggers), and resolve opt-out by the canonical customerId/phone rather than by the raw key.
findings.reason: Confirmed: runAutomationServerSide and dispatchSettlement fallback call messagingService.sendMessage which uses driver.sendText directly; no isSuppressed (conversations.optedOut) check and not counted under maxPerDay (only maxPerRun). triggerSettlementMessage/buildSnapshotForKey has no opt-out check.

findings.title: Lapsed / high-spend / milestone rules re-fire every day forever for the same customers
findings.detail: evaluateRule's INACTIVITY (`daysSinceLastVisit >= days`), HIGH_SPEND (`totalSpend >= threshold`) and VISIT_MILESTONE (`totalVisits === milestone`) conditions stay true until the customer's next visit. evaluateDefaultTriggers and customerAutomationService.evaluateTrigger (WIN_BACK >= 30 days) work the same way. The only dedup is same-IST-day (recentJob here; enqueueWhatsApp / hasBeenMessagedToday in the hourly engine). Nothing records 'already sent WIN_BACK/INACTIVITY to this customer for this lapse', and no N-day cooldown exists anywhere in server/services. The seeded defaults (INACTIVITY 30/14, HIGH_SPEND 10000, VISIT_MILESTONE 10) are active on first boot.
findings.failure_scenario: A customer last visited 40 days ago. With automation enabled, every day at 10am the rule engine sends them a win-back offer, and the hourly engine queues WIN_BACK again each new day. A ₹10k+ lifetime customer gets 'complimentary starter' every day. This continues until they return, which is exactly the send volume CLAUDE.md warns gets numbers banned.
findings.suggested_fix: Before sending, check automation_jobs for a sent job of the same trigger/rule for this customerId since their last order (or within a configurable cooldown, e.g. 14-30 days). Apply the same check in customerAutomationService.runCustomerAutomation.
findings.reason: Confirmed: evaluateDefaultTriggers/evaluateRule conditions are threshold-based (>= days, >= spend) and only same-IST-day dedup exists (recentJob, enqueueWhatsApp, hasBeenMessagedToday); grep found no cooldown anywhere. A lapsed customer gets INACTIVITY_7 / INACTIVITY_14 / WIN_BACK every day while automation is enabled.

findings.title: Daily rule engine and hourly engine dedup on different keys, so a customer can get two re-engagement messages the same day
findings.detail: runAutomationServerSide skips if ANY job for the customerId has scheduledAt >= today. The hourly runCustomerAutomation enqueues through enqueueWhatsApp, which only blocks the SAME triggerType. The rule engine stores the DB rule's triggerType ('INACTIVITY', 'HIGH_SPEND', ...), while the hourly engine uses 'WIN_BACK'/'AT_RISK'.
findings.failure_scenario: At 10:00 the rule engine sends 'INACTIVITY' to a 35-day-lapsed customer. At the next hourly tick, enqueueWhatsApp finds no same-day 'WIN_BACK' job and queues a second win-back message to the same person.
findings.suggested_fix: Make enqueueWhatsApp's same-day check trigger-agnostic for re-engagement triggers (any sent/pending job for the customer today), or share one dedup helper between both engines.
findings.reason: Confirmed: hourly engine dedups via file-log hasBeenMessagedToday (rule engine writes customer_messages, not the file log) and enqueueWhatsApp keyed on same triggerType; rule engine stores rule triggerType (INACTIVITY etc.) vs hourly WIN_BACK/AT_RISK, so rule-engine-first then hourly enqueues a second message the same day.

findings.title: Hourly automation run downloads the entire orders, order_items and menu_items tables
findings.detail: buildCustomerProfiles runs `db.select().from(orders)` with no filter, plus `db.select().from(orderItems)` and `db.select().from(menuItems)` (all columns), on every scheduled run (every runIntervalHours, default 1h, whenever automation is enabled). order_items is larger than orders, which alone was ~500 KB per read in Oct 2026. automationRuleEngine.buildSnapshots (line 221) does the same unfiltered orders read daily. CLAUDE.md's egress rules forbid reading the whole orders table on a recurring path.
findings.failure_scenario: With automation enabled, 24 runs a day × (orders + order_items + menu_items) is tens of MB a day of Supabase egress that grows with history, which is the same failure mode as the Oct 2026 quota blow-out.
findings.suggested_fix: Aggregate per customer in SQL (count, sum, max(created_at) grouped by phone/name, filtered to status <> 'cancelled'). Fetch favourite items only for the customers that actually hit a trigger, selecting just the needed columns.
findings.reason: Confirmed: buildCustomerProfiles selects all orders, all order_items, all menu_items every run (scheduled hourly, gated only by config.enabled); buildSnapshots reads all orders daily. Violates CLAUDE.md egress rule.

findings.title: resolveCustomerId called without a phone from logging/loyalty paths creates duplicate customers_master rows and splits customer identity
findings.detail: logToDb calls resolveCustomerId(customerKey, customerName) with no phone. eventService.logMessageSentEvent/logMilestone (no phone), loyaltyService.earnPointsForOrder/redeemPoints (`null` phone) and segmentation's milestone log do the same. resolveCustomerId's phone fallback (step 2) runs only when a phone is passed, so a key that is a phone number but whose canonical master row is keyed by name falls through to step 3 and INSERTs a new row with key=<phone>, phone=NULL. From then on, step 1's exact-key match returns this duplicate for every caller using the phone key. automation_jobs dedup, customer_segments and customer_profiles (where a STOP opt-out was recorded against the original id) now point at different ids.
findings.failure_scenario: A customer was created by name 'Asha' and her phone was later linked (master key 'Asha', phone 98xxxxxxxx). Orders now carry the phone, so key = phone. The first settlement's earnPointsForOrder(phone, 'Asha') inserts a second master row keyed by the phone. Next morning buildSnapshots looks up the profile by masterMap.get(phone), gets the duplicate with no profile, and her doNotSendUpdate opt-out on the original row is ignored. Segments and today's-job dedup also split.
findings.suggested_fix: In resolveCustomerId, when `phone` is not given and `key` is 10+ digits, use the key as the phone for the step-2 fallback. Also pass the real phone from logToDb, the eventService wrappers and loyaltyService.
findings.reason: Confirmed: logToDb, logMessageSentEvent/logMilestone, loyaltyService (null phone) skip resolveCustomerId's phone fallback; when the canonical row is name-keyed with a backfilled phone (CRM profile save / step-1 backfill), a phone-key lookup without phone inserts a duplicate key=phone row which step 1 then returns for all later callers.

findings.title: WATI and MSG91 senders treat any 10-digit number starting with '91' as already country-coded
findings.detail: sendWhatsAppWATI and sendSMS use `normalised.startsWith('91') ? normalised : '91'+normalised`. This is the exact bug CLAUDE.md records as fixed in normalizePhone/normalizeWaPhone: a genuine mobile like 9187654321 is sent as the 10-digit '9187654321' instead of '919187654321'.
findings.failure_scenario: With WATI configured (no driver), a due reminder or automation message to a customer whose number is 9187654321 is posted to /sendSessionMessage/9187654321, which fails or goes to the wrong number. The same happens for MSG91 SMS.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse normalizeWaPhone (length-based: 10 → prepend 91, 12 starting 91 → keep, 11 with leading 0 → strip and prepend).
findings.reason: Confirmed: sendWhatsAppWATI and sendSMS use startsWith('91') — the exact bug CLAUDE.md records fixed elsewhere. Reachable only when WATI/MSG91 are configured.

findings.title: backfillOrderPhone stamps a phone onto every phone-less order of anyone sharing the same name
findings.detail: Saving a CRM profile with a phone runs backfillOrderPhone(key, name, phone), which updates every order where `lower(customer_name) = lower(key or name)` and phone is empty. Walk-in names ('Raj', 'Guest', 'Amit') are shared by unrelated people, so their orders are reassigned to this phone. getOpenTabsByCustomer, the Dues e-bill, CRM snapshots, segmentation and loyalty all group by phone afterwards. CLAUDE.md already flags name-only matching as wrong when a phone is available (buildSnapshotForKey fix).
findings.failure_scenario: Staff add phone 98xxxxxxxx to the customer 'Raj'. Months of other 'Raj' walk-ins' orders, including another Raj's unpaid due tab, now carry that phone. The consolidated e-bill sent to this customer lists another person's outstanding orders and total, and his visit count/VIP status is inflated.
findings.suggested_fix: Limit the backfill to orders positively tied to this customer (e.g. ids the user selected, or orders already linked to this customers_master id), or at least require confirmation and restrict it to the exact key with an order-count preview.
findings.reason: Confirmed code does name-only mass backfill on CRM profile save. Downgraded: name-keyed customers are already aggregated by name across the CRM, so the backfill is consistent with that identity model; still an irreversible write onto unrelated walk-ins sharing a common name.

findings.title: CRM aggregates (segments, settlement snapshot, rule-engine snapshot) count cancelled orders as visits and spend
findings.detail: runSegmentationForCustomer, buildSnapshotForKey (customerAutomationService.ts:205), buildCustomerProfiles and automationRuleEngine.buildSnapshots sum totalAmount and count rows over all of a customer's orders with no `status <> 'cancelled'` filter (and without netting shortfallAmount). CLAUDE.md: any aggregate over orders must exclude cancelled.
findings.failure_scenario: A new customer's first order is cancelled and re-rung. At settlement, buildSnapshotForKey sees totalVisits=2, so instead of WELCOME they get the returning-customer THANK_YOU 'for dining with us again'. A customer whose only order was cancelled gets win-back messages 30 days later, and cancelled high-value test orders can push someone into VIP.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `ne(orders.status, 'cancelled')` (and ideally exclude 'hold') to each of these order queries, and use totalAmount − shortfallAmount for spend.
findings.reason: Confirmed: runSegmentationForCustomer, buildSnapshotForKey, buildCustomerProfiles and buildSnapshots have no status <> 'cancelled' filter or shortfall netting; CLAUDE.md requires every aggregate over orders to exclude cancelled.

findings.title: Hourly batch segmentation is an unconditional N+1 over every distinct (phone,name) pair, and skips name-only customers whose phone is ''
findings.detail: startSegmentationScheduler(1) is started unconditionally in server/index.ts (it doesn't check automation enabled). For every distinct (key,name,phone) row it runs resolveCustomerId (1-3 queries, possibly an INSERT), an unindexed `customer_phone = key OR customer_name = key` scan of orders, a segment SELECT and an UPSERT, all sequentially, every hour. A customer with several name spellings is processed once per spelling. COALESCE(phone, name) yields '' when the phone is stored as an empty string, which `if (!row.key)` then skips, so those customers' recency never decays to At Risk/Lapsed in the batch.
findings.failure_scenario: With ~500 customers, each hour issues ~2,000+ sequential queries including ~500 sequential scans of orders, against the shared Supabase DB. A name-only regular whose phone is '' stays 'Regular' forever and never appears in the digest's at-risk count.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute RFM for all customers in one grouped SQL query keyed on NULLIF(trim(phone),'') / name, then batch-upsert segments. Use COALESCE(NULLIF(phone,''), name).
findings.reason: Confirmed: startSegmentationScheduler(1) is unconditional in server/index.ts; sequential per-(key,name,phone) resolve + OR scan + upsert; COALESCE('', name) yields '' and POS saves customerPhone as '' when blank, so those name-only customers are skipped.

findings.title: VISIT_MILESTONE event re-logged every hour while a customer sits at 5/10/25/50 visits
findings.detail: `if ([5,10,25,50].includes(visits)) await logMilestone(...)` runs on every call, including each hourly runSegmentationForAll, not just when the visit count changes.
findings.failure_scenario: A customer with exactly 10 orders gets a new MILESTONE event every hour (24/day) until their next visit, which bloats customer_events and makes the timeline/analytics show repeated milestones.
findings.suggested_fix: Log the milestone only when the visit count reaches the threshold on order creation (compare with the previous count), or check for an existing MILESTONE event with the same value.
findings.reason: Confirmed: logMilestone runs whenever visits is in [5,10,25,50], including every hourly batch; logEventByKey has no dedup.

findings.title: Favourite item ignores order_items.name, so open items become a favourite called 'Unknown'
findings.detail: buildCustomerProfiles and buildSnapshotForKey (line 241) resolve names only via menuNameMap[item.menuItemId] ?? 'Unknown'. Open items (negative ids) and any item without a menu row all collapse into one 'Unknown' bucket, whose combined quantity can win. CLAUDE.md requires preferring order_items.name.
findings.failure_scenario: A regular whose recent orders include a few open items ('Special Thali' typed manually) settles a bill. In 'auto' mode the tag is Regular with favoriteItem 'Unknown', so they receive 'We know you love *Unknown* at Bagicha!'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `item.name ?? menuNameMap[item.menuItemId]` and skip lines with no resolvable name (or with menuItemId < 0) when picking a favourite.
findings.reason: Confirmed: both favourite computations use menuNameMap[item.menuItemId] ?? 'Unknown' ignoring orderItems.name; the result feeds FAVORITE_ITEM settlement messages, so a customer can be told their favourite is 'Unknown'.

findings.title: Hourly engine's legacy send path checks only the file-based opt-out, not the DB STOP flag
findings.detail: When whatsappAutoSend is off (or no driver), runCustomerAutomation gates on isOptedOut(customer.key) (automationStore's JSON prefs) and then calls sendWhatsAppMessage via Meta/WATI. The STOP keyword sets conversations.optedOut and customer_profiles.doNotSendUpdate in the DB, which this path never reads.
findings.failure_scenario: With Meta Cloud API configured and autoSend off, a customer who replied STOP is still sent a WIN_BACK message after 30 days of inactivity.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the legacy send, check the same DB suppression outboundQueue.isSuppressed uses (conversations.optedOut by normalized phone, and doNotSendUpdate for the resolved customerId).
findings.reason: Confirmed: legacy path in runCustomerAutomation checks only automationStore isOptedOut (file prefs) and sends via Meta/WATI; STOP handling writes conversations.optedOut and customer_profiles.doNotSendUpdate which this path never reads.

findings.title: Owner's daily digest counts cancelled orders as revenue and due, ignores write-offs, and treats still-open orders as due
findings.detail: dayOrders has no status filter. totalRevenue/avgOrderValue/totalOrders include cancelled orders, and dueRevenue (`paymentStatus === 'pending'`) includes every cancelled order (cancel doesn't change paymentStatus) plus every running table / held order that simply hasn't been settled yet at digest time (default 23:00). topItems (line 95-107) also includes cancelled orders' items. Revenue isn't net of shortfallAmount, unlike Reports. CLAUDE.md: cancelled orders are not sales, and revenue nets write-offs.
findings.failure_scenario: On a day with one ₹1,200 cancelled order, two tables still running at 23:00 (₹1,800) and a ₹50 write-off, the WhatsApp digest overstates Revenue by ₹1,250 and shows 'Due: ₹3,000' although no customer owes anything. It also disagrees with Reports for the same day.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter `status <> 'cancelled'` for revenue/orders/top items, compute revenue as totalAmount − shortfallAmount, and define Due as status='served' AND paymentStatus='pending' (isDueOrder).
findings.reason: Confirmed: dayOrders has no status filter; dueRevenue = paymentStatus pending includes cancelled and open/held orders; topItems not filtered; no shortfall netting. Downgraded to medium: owner digest figures only, no money is moved.

findings.title: 'Slow movers' are lifetime totals, not today's, and include deleted items
findings.detail: worstItems left-joins orders with the date window in the join condition, but sums orderItems.quantity, which is joined unconditionally. Order items from any date are counted, so the ranking is all-time sales. It also filters only isAvailable, not isDeleted.
findings.failure_scenario: An item that sold 0 today but 500 lifetime never appears as a slow mover, while a soft-deleted dish with few lifetime sales is reported to the owner as today's slow mover.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the date filter on an inner join/subquery of today's order items (e.g. sum(CASE WHEN orders.id IS NOT NULL THEN qty END)), and add `isDeleted = false`.
findings.reason: Confirmed: date bounds sit in the orders left-join condition but orderItems quantity is summed unconditionally, so it is lifetime; filters isAvailable only, not isDeleted.

findings.title: Overlapping minute ticks double-send feedback requests; failed rows are retried every minute forever and can starve the queue
findings.detail: dailyScheduler uses setInterval(tick, 60s) with no re-entrancy guard, and tick awaits processPendingFeedback. That function selects up to 50 rows with sentAt IS NULL (no ORDER BY, no claim) and sends them sequentially with a 1 s pause plus API latency. With a backlog of ~40+ rows one pass exceeds 60 s, so the next tick selects the same unsent rows and sends them again. A row whose send fails (invalid/non-WhatsApp number) keeps sentAt NULL and has no attempt counter, so it is retried every minute indefinitely. 50 such rows fill the LIMIT and block new ones.
findings.failure_scenario: After enabling feedback (or after downtime) with 60 eligible paid orders, customers in the overlap window receive the rating request twice. A handful of numbers that Meta rejects are re-posted 1,440 times a day each, and once 50 accumulate, no new feedback request is ever sent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an isRunning guard to processPendingFeedback (or tick). Claim rows atomically (e.g. UPDATE … SET sent_at = now() … RETURNING, or a 'sending' status) before sending. Record attempts/last error, stop after N failures, and ORDER BY created_at.
findings.reason: Confirmed: setInterval tick without re-entrancy guard awaits processPendingFeedback; 50-row LIMIT with no ORDER BY/claim, 1s pacing per row. sendWhatsAppMessage returns success:false for an invalid phone, sentAt stays NULL with no attempt counter, so such rows retry every minute forever and can fill the LIMIT.

findings.title: Feedback requests ignore customer opt-out
findings.detail: scheduleFeedbackForOrder and sendFeedbackMessage never check customer_profiles.doNotSendUpdate/notificationEnabled, conversations.optedOut or automationStore.isOptedOut before sending via sendWhatsAppMessage.
findings.failure_scenario: A customer who replied STOP (or was marked 'do not send updates' by staff) still gets a 'rate your experience' WhatsApp after every paid order.
findings.suggested_fix: Before sending, apply the same suppression check the outbound queue uses (by normalized phone and resolved customerId), and mark the row skipped.
findings.reason: Confirmed: no opt-out check in scheduleFeedbackForOrder, processPendingFeedback or sendFeedbackMessage.

findings.title: Feedback delay is measured from order creation, not payment
findings.detail: The header says 'now() >= order.paidAt + delayMinutes', but the query uses `lte(orders.createdAt, cutoff)`. orders.paid_at exists and is stamped at settlement.
findings.failure_scenario: A table opened at 7:00 pm and settled at 9:30 pm with a 120-minute delay gets the feedback request within a minute of paying, while the guests are still at the table.
findings.suggested_fix: Use coalesce(orders.paid_at, orders.created_at) <= cutoff.
findings.reason: Confirmed: query uses lte(orders.createdAt, cutoff) while paid_at exists; a long-running table settled after the delay gets the request immediately after paying.

findings.title: Feedback link is a bare relative path when no base URL is configured
findings.detail: buildFeedbackUrl returns `/feedback/<token>` when both feedbackBaseUrl and trackingBaseUrl are empty, and that relative path is sent in the WhatsApp message (and the row is marked sent).
findings.failure_scenario: With feedback enabled but no base URL set, every customer receives a non-clickable '/feedback/abc…' link. No ratings can come back, yet the requests are recorded as sent.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse to send (log/skip) when no absolute base URL is configured, or require the base URL when feedbackEnabled is turned on.
findings.reason: Confirmed: feedbackBaseUrl and trackingBaseUrl default to '' in automationStore, producing a relative '/feedback/<token>' link in the WhatsApp message.

findings.title: Co-purchase scoring can never score anything, so 'upsells' are arbitrary (possibly deleted) menu items
findings.detail: coFreq only counts items b from the customer's own orders where `!orderedIds.has(b)`, but every non-open item in those orders is in orderedIds by construction, so coFreq stays empty. upsells then become the first 3 of an unordered `LIMIT 20` menu query, labelled 'Co-purchased'. That query filters isAvailable but not isDeleted.
findings.failure_scenario: The CRM profile suggests random dishes as 'Co-purchased' upsells, including soft-deleted items the restaurant no longer serves.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute co-purchase across all customers' orders (items co-occurring with this customer's top items), order the menu candidates by restaurant popularity, and add `isDeleted = false`.
findings.reason: Confirmed: every positive menuItemId in the customer's own orders is in orderedIds, so coFreq only gains entries for negative open-item ids never in the menu; upsells are the first 3 of an unordered LIMIT 20 without isDeleted filter, labelled Co-purchased.

findings.title: Customer message history returns the oldest 50 messages, not the latest
findings.detail: getCustomerMessages orders by createdAt ascending with LIMIT 50.
findings.failure_scenario: For a customer with more than 50 logged messages, GET /api/crm/customers/:key/messages never shows anything recent: the latest settlement/due messages are missing from the history.
findings.suggested_fix: orderBy(desc(customerMessages.createdAt)).limit(limit), reversed client-side if chronological display is needed.
findings.reason: Confirmed: orderBy(createdAt) ascending + LIMIT 50, used by the CRM messages route; returns oldest 50 once history exceeds 50.

findings.title: Consolidated e-bill does 3 sequential queries per order, including a full menu read each time
findings.detail: sendConsolidatedEbill loops orderIds and awaits buildOrderBillBlock for each. Each call re-reads the order (already known to the caller), its items, and `SELECT id,name FROM menu_items` for the whole menu. triggerDueBillMessage also reads the order twice (line 627 and inside buildOrderBillBlock).
findings.failure_scenario: Sending an e-bill for a customer with 8 open tabs makes ~24 serial round trips (8 full menu reads) before the owner's tap returns, several seconds on the shop's ~100 ms RTT path.
findings.suggested_fix: Fetch all orders and items for orderIds in two queries, left-join menu_items for names, and build the blocks in memory.
findings.reason: Confirmed: buildOrderBillBlock re-reads order, items and the full menu per order; triggerDueBillMessage reads the order twice. Performance only.

findings.title: Every settlement runs a regex sequential scan of orders and a full menu_items read
findings.detail: buildSnapshotForKey filters on `right(regexp_replace(coalesce(customer_phone,''),'\D','','g'),10) = $1` (not indexable, so it evaluates the regex on every order row), selects all columns, and then reads `SELECT * FROM menu_items` just to map names for ≤5 orders.
findings.failure_scenario: Each paid settlement (when automation is enabled) does a full scan of orders plus a full menu read in the background on the shared DB, costing egress and load that grow with history.
findings.suggested_fix: Select only id/totalAmount/createdAt/customerName/customerPhone, and resolve item names via a leftJoin on just the top-5 orders' items. Consider a normalized-phone expression index.
findings.reason: Confirmed: non-sargable regex predicate over orders, SELECT * plus full menu_items read per settlement. Performance only.

findings.title: One failing person/day group aborts the rest of a punch batch
findings.detail: The single try/catch wraps the whole groups loop, so an exception for one group (e.g. a DB error in replaceAutoShiftSessions) stops processing of every later group. The status becomes 'failed' even though earlier rows were written. The 'partial' status is never produced.
findings.failure_scenario: A sync batch covering 10 staff hits an error on the 3rd person, and the remaining 7 people's punches for that batch are not recorded until the device data is re-sent.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the try/catch inside the loop, record per-group errors, and set status 'partial' when some groups succeeded.
findings.reason: Confirmed: single try/catch around the groups loop; route returns 200 with status 'failed', and attendanceAgent treats res.ok as synced and drops its buffer, so later groups' punches in that batch are lost. Requires a DB error mid-batch.
